title: Product Hub: Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap, Pricing, Release Notes - Unified Inference
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose
-----
This document is the canonical product hub for the Unified Inference product area: it consolidates the high-level product overview, the current PRD and core requirements, design specifications for major components, roadmap & themes for the next three quarters, pricing & packaging guidance, and the most recent release notes. The goal is to provide a single, readable reference for engineering, sales, support, and customers who have access to internal docs.

Summary / TL;DR
----------------
- Product: Unified Inference — single API and control plane for hosted, dedicated, and private inference deployments.
- Primary goals: predictable latency & throughput, cost-aware controls, consistent developer UX across environments.
- Next major focus (Q1–Q2 2027): dedicated autoscaling & billing-integrated cost controls + VPC private deployment GA.

1) Product overview
--------------------
Short intro: Unified Inference provides a single developer-facing API and operational surface that lets teams run text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking across Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private with consistent semantics, SLAs, and observability.

Key capabilities (current):
- Model catalog with verified performance profiles (p95 latency, throughput, memory) for curated open models.
- Streaming responses, function/tool calling primitives, structured output support (JSON schema enforcement at SDK level).
- Intelligent routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-pref) with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Automatic prefix & KV caching, workload-aware batching, and quantization profile recommendations via Redwood Optimize.
- Per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost attribution, and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback).

SLOs and targets:
- Request-level latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for small-chat (<= 128 tokens) on Hosted API in primary regions.
- Throughput SLO for Dedicated: sustained 10k tokens/sec per reserved GPU pool (example baseline).
- Error budget policy: 99.95% availability monthly target for Dedicated customers on paid SLAs.

Primary personas and JTBD (jobs-to-be-done):
- Product engineers: add LLM features with predictable latency and cost.
- ML/platform engineers: standardize inference across teams and hardware.
- Infra/security: deploy private inference with compliance controls.

2) PRD summary & core requirements
----------------------------------
Objective: Deliver GA of Dedicated autoscaling with integrated cost controls and rollout policies, plus VPC Private deployment GA with automated upgrade/rollback flows.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Adoption: 20 customers onboarded to Dedicated autoscaling within 60 days of GA.
- Cost efficiency: 15% reduction in median per-token cost for customers using recommended batching/caching profiles.
- Reliability: Meet Dedicated SLA for 3 consecutive months (99.95% availability).

Core functional requirements (MUST):
1. Autoscaling policy engine that supports metrics-based scaling (latency, queue length, throughput) with configurable min/max capacity per pool.
2. Billing integration that meters token consumption per-pool and calculates committed vs. overage charges per billing cycle.
3. Route-level cost controls: per-route cost ceiling and automated fallback to cheaper model variants when thresholds are exceeded.
4. Private VPC deployment: customer-controlled control plane connectivity, KMS integration, and audit logging to customer SIEM.
5. Upgrade & rollback: zero-downtime bundle upgrades for Private with health checks and automatic rollback on regression signals.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- Autoscaler decisions converge within 90s for ramping workloads.
- End-to-end encrypted data-in-transit and at-rest for Private deployments.
- Observability: 1s resolution traces for sampling important token streams; 99% of traces available in console within 10 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (example):
- E2E test harness demonstrates autoscaler increases capacity under sustained 5x baseline load and reduces when load drops to baseline within configured cooldowns.
- Billing metrics are exported to finance pipeline with <1% discrepancy vs. internal accounting for a representative sample month.

Requirements table (concise)
| Requirement ID | Short description | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| RQ-100 | Autoscaling policy engine (latency/queue) | MUST | eng-platform | Autoscale up/down per policy within 90s under load tests |
| RQ-110 | Per-route cost ceilings and fallback | MUST | eng-serving-runtime | Route falls back and logs event when cost ceiling reached in integration test |
| RQ-120 | Billing integration for Dedicated | MUST | finance-legal / eng-infra | Metering + invoice generation tested on staging |
| RQ-130 | Private VPC GA | MUST | eng-private-deployments | Customer CI verifies control plane connectivity + KMS |

3) Design specs (high-level)
----------------------------
Architecture overview (text diagram):
- API Gateway -> Router (policy evaluation) -> Model Proxy Layer -> Serving Runtime (GPU pools / CPU fallbacks) -> KV Cache (shared caching layer) -> Metrics/Tracing -> Billing + Observability services.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Centralized Router for policy evaluation: simplifies cross-cutting policies (cost, region, latency) and enables consistent logging for audits.
- Model Proxy Layer: abstracts model variant compatibility and handles automatic conversion (quantized variants, shorter context window fallbacks).
- KV cache placement: colocate cache shards with GPU pools to minimize cross-network latency for hot prefixes.

Interfaces & contracts (selected):
- Router policy API: JSON policy objects (example in appendix) that evaluate on request metadata and runtime signals.
- Autoscaler telemetry: exposes open metrics: inference_queue_length, avg_latency_30s, tokens_per_sec, node_utilization.

Operational considerations:
- Canary rollouts: 10% traffic for first 12 hours -> 30% for next 24 hours -> 100% after 72 hours if no regressions. Automated rollback triggers on +5% token error rate or +20ms p95 latency regression vs. baseline.
- Failure modes: overloaded cache shard fallback behavior will route to cold path with increased latency and emit cost/latency signals to router for dynamic routing adjustments.

4) Roadmap & themes (3-quarter view)
------------------------------------
Quarterly themes: Q1 2027 (GA readiness), Q2 2027 (scale & ops), Q3 2027 (enterprise polish).
Roadmap bullets: 
- Q1 2027: Dedicated autoscaler GA, billing integration MVP, Private VPC GA beta.
- Q2 2027: Autoscaler policy templates, rollout automation for Dedicated (canary A/B), console UX for cost ceilings per-route, extended regional coverage (APAC).
- Q3 2027: Enterprise features: SLA-based placement, audit export pipelines, advanced eviction policies for KV cache, Marketplace connectors for model catalog.

Dependencies and risks:
- Depend on eng-infra for additional GPU capacity and networking for Dedicated pools (risk: capacity shortage delays GA).
- Depend on finance-legal to finalize contract model for committed capacity and overage pricing (risk: pricing freeze impacts go-to-market).

5) Pricing and packaging notes
-----------------------------
Packaging tiers (draft):
- Hosted API (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token + optional Optimize add-on.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commit for GPU pools + per-token usage for burst. Two SKUs: Standard Dedicated (no SLA) and SLA Dedicated (99.95% uptime + premium support).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform license fee + deployment support package + optional managed upgrades.

Pricing guidance (example):
- Hosted: $0.0009 / generation token (baseline open LLM), embeddings $0.0005 / unit (example).
- Dedicated: capacity commit priced per GPU-hour equivalent; example: $X per vGPU-hr with graduated discounts for 6/12/24-month terms. Overage priced at 120% of committed unit rate.

Cost controls & discounts:
- Recommend bundling Redwood Optimize with Dedicated for customers looking to hit aggressive cost targets (batching + caching recommendations typically reduce unit cost by 10–25%).
- Volume discounts tiers at 10TB/month token volume and 3 higher tiers. Exact numbers pending finance-legal review.

Sales & packaging playbook (high-level):
1. Discovery: measure customer latency and token volume; recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
2. Pilot: 30–90 day pilot on Dedicated with capacity commit option; include 90-day trial of Redwood Optimize.
3. Scale: convert to commit term with SLA + platform support.

6) Release notes (most recent release: 2026-12-01)
---------------------------------------------------
Release: Unified Inference v2026-12-01 (internal GA candidates)
Highlights:
- Added per-route cost ceilings + automatic fallback to compatible cheaper model variant.
- Router policy API v1 launched with support for region-pref and latency-first policies.
- Initial Dedicated autoscaler alpha: supports queue-length and latency-based scaling with simple cooldowns.
- Private VPC: control plane connectivity and KMS integration prototype validated in three internal customers.

Bug fixes and minor changes:
- Fixed cache eviction leading to hot-shard skew under synthetic workloads.
- Improved tracing correlation IDs for multi-hop proxy flows.

Known issues:
- Autoscaler can oscillate with very bursty micro-bursts; mitigation: increase cooldown or enable smoothed metrics (upstream work planned).
- Billing export lag can be up to 30 minutes in staging; production target is 5 minutes.

Rollout plan for this release:
1. Internal dogfood (1 day): routing 100% internal traffic through new Router policy API.
2. Canary customers (3 customers for 2 weeks): enable per-route cost ceilings and autoscaler alpha.
3. Gradual expansion: widen to up to 50 customers in next month depending on telemetry.

7) Operational runbook pointers (short)
-------------------------------------
- Incidents impacting Router: paging list -> eng-platform -> eng-serving-runtime -> SRE on-call.
- Key dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), autoscaler events, cost-ceil breaches, cache hit ratio.
- Troubleshooting checklist: verify policy evaluation logs, inspect node utilization, check KV cache health endpoints, escalate to core serving runtime if GPU OOMs observed.
